_comment: Industry context for the Market page ('Industry' tab). 'germanyMonthly' is refreshed automatically from DIE PAPIERINDUSTRIE's monthly 'Statistische Kurzinformation' (scripts/collect_industry.py). The other blocks are yearly figures, updated by hand (see prompts/peers-update-prompt.md, part 'Industry').

latestNote.text: First half of 2026: hygiene paper production 658,000 t (−2.0 %), demand for hygiene papers flat (±0 %).

source.label: DIE PAPIERINDUSTRIE, Paper Facts and Figures 2026

about.what: Year-to-date production and sales of German paper mills by main grade, published monthly by the German paper industry association. Hygiene papers = tissue base paper produced on paper machines.
about.wepa: The size and direction of WEPA's home market for tissue. A falling production volume with stable demand means more imports – more competition for German mills.
about.limits: Machine production of tissue base paper, not converted products or WEPA's own volumes. Year-to-date totals, so early-year changes can swing. Covers German mills only.

germanyRecoveredRate.label: Recovered paper utilisation rate by paper grade, Germany

source.label: Umweltbundesamt, based on DIE PAPIERINDUSTRIE, Leistungsbericht PAPIER 2025

wepaRef.label: WEPA recycled fibre share 2025
wepaRef.note: share of the fibre portfolio by sold volume – a different definition, see below

about.what: Recovered paper used per tonne of paper produced, by grade, in Germany (recovered paper consumption ÷ production). Values above 100 % mean more recovered paper goes in than paper comes out, because of losses in recycling.
about.wepa: The German tissue industry has been using less recovered paper for years (53 % in 2010, 39 % in 2024) – it is moving towards fresh fibre, while WEPA aims for 60 % recycled and alternative fibres by 2030. That makes WEPA's recycled strategy a differentiator, but also means less industry demand pulling deinking grades into tissue.
about.limits: Not directly comparable with WEPA's 31.8 %: WEPA measures the share of recycled fibre in its sold products, while this rate measures recovered paper input (including losses) per tonne of paper. Yearly, with about a year's delay.

about.what: Key figures of the European pulp and paper industry from Cepi, the European association, published once a year (July).
about.wepa: The European backdrop: shrinking graphic papers, more imports and falling CO₂ intensity. Tissue is not shown separately in the summary, but import penetration and capacity closures affect the competitive situation for WEPA's mills.
about.limits: Cepi member countries, yearly, about six months after year-end. No tissue-specific figures in the summary.
